feature_sentence: As a user, I want support summary component in another step.
documentation_text:
Source: https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/996

State: CLOSED

Labels: kind/user-story, feature-complete, area/summary

Description:
### Description
Currently it is not really possible to use `Summary` on a confirmation step. In the examples in the documentation, a new component that is readOnly is instead used. We would rather like to support the summary view. The problem with this currently, is that the layout of the data step is not available, and so there is no natural `componentRef`.

It is not obvious how this should be solved, some alternatives are:
1. Configure a "new" component, and somehow set its rendering mode to summary instead.
  - Simple "renderAsSummary": true.
2. Have the summary component refer to the datamodel instead of a different component.
  - Challenges: how do you configure the component settings.
3. Reference the layout and components of a previous step
4. Render summary when the task-type is confirmation.
  - Challenges: Goes against our wish to make tasks less "type dependent".

After a brief discussion we agreed to move on with alternative 1. This means we are extending the the actual components with a summary mode in addition to read and write. At the same time pushing some of the summary component specific settings that exists today until we know more about the needs.

Summary on a separate task than the one used to fill in the data serves a slightly different purpose than having a summary as the last page of a form. On the last page of a form the purpose is to quickly review the form and the values allowing to go back and correct the values. Summary on later step is about reviewing the data in order to make a decision and you might not even av access to modify the data. A decision in this case is to sign or reject based on the values provided effectively moving the process.

### Additional Information
- Edit options should be disabled as the previous step is completed. Other actions might set the process back allowing for editing. But the summary on a confirm step should probably be read only.

### Tasks
- [x] Identify all components that should have a summary mode
- [ ] Implement summary mode on identified components
- [ ] Document the setup and configuration and any differences with regards to the summary component

### Acceptance Criterias
- [ ] Ability to create a layout with components setting the mode to summary
- [ ] Trying to pass data updates to the server should return a Forbidden response

feature_sentence: As a user, I want support for shadow fields in app form.
documentation_text:
Source: https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/744

State: CLOSED

Labels: area/data-storage, kind/user-story, org/brg, org/ssb, status/draft, feature-complete

Description:
### Description

We currently only support storing data in the data model. If a shadow field is required to f.ex. store some data needed for f.ex. dynamics in the form, this needs to be part of the data model and as such will also be submitted with the final data (unless app developer writes some custom code to scrub out this kind of data).

We should support the concept of shadow fields, that is, fields that can contain data, but are not connected to the data model in any way.

### Additional Information

A first try at defining how we can support this.
- Shadow fields should be stored as flat key/value pairs.
  - Naming convention from frontend could be `<page>.<componentId>`, to make sure keys are unique.
- No model connection, so would have to be deserialized to f.ex. a dictionary with string values in order to be used in any server-side calculations. 
  - App developer needs to know the keys that are used
- Frontend components - formData:
  - If no dataModelBindings are present for the component, use naming convention for shadow field to read/write data.
  - If dataModelBindings are present, these are used instead
- API - probably need new endpoint to save/fetch shadow field data.
  - For a POC, we could just add a new data type in `applicationMetadata` and use a naming convention, so that we can store/fetch the data using existing data endpoint.

The outlined solution supports rendering forms without any data model connection. It also supports a hybrid solution where some fields are connected to data model while others are true shadow fields. 
One issue is that it could be difficult to validate the data submitted as shadow  fields.

Alternative: Generate a data model from UI schema. This would enforce a contract of WHAT can be submitted/stored as a helper field, and allow for full deserialization and intellisense on server level. In this case we could have the same implementation frontend as suggested above.

### Open questions
- [ ] Where do we store this type of data? 
  - One set of shadow fields stored per instance? Per data element/task?
- [ ] Should the data be stored after the instance is submitted/archived?
- [ ] Store data as flat key/value pair list with no data model, or generate data model?

### Tasks

- [ ] Decide on implementation
- [ ] POC

### Acceptance Criterias

- Possible to render a form and store/fetch data without connecting fields to a data model.
- Possible to enter/store helper data that is not submitted with the rest of the form data
- Possible to use values in helper fields in server-side calculations/validations

feature_sentence: As a user, I want dynamic codelists not working in repeatable groups.
As a user, I want improve loading logic in app frontend.
documentation_text:
Source: https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/121

State: CLOSED

Labels: quality/debt, kind/user-story

Description:
## Description
We seem to have a problem with a race condition in our loading logic of app frontend. Seems to be specifically tied to stateless apps, and was made obvious after implementation of anonymous stateless frontend.

When app loads, it checks if the app has `allowAnonymous` condition set via selector. This requires both applicationMetadata and layoutSets. The call to load these is triggered from App.tsx. Once these are loaded, App re-renders with final value for `allowAnonymous`.

While this is happening, Entrypoint.tsx is also rendering. If app is configured as stateless, call to start statelessQueue is triggered - _if `state.isLoading.stateless === null`. This value is updated to `true` once the queue is triggered, and this is used to make sure we don't trigger the queue more than once.
At this point, it seems that App reloads before `state.isLoading.stateless` has been updated, leading to new calls to trigger the queue. This results in an indefinite reload-loop which breaks the frontend.

We need to think about how we can simplify this loading logic so that we avoid this issue. A workaround has been made for a temporary fix, see considerations.

## Considerations
A temporary workaround has been to make sure `allowAnonymous` is determined in App.tsx before we do any loading of Entrypoint.

Description:
## Description
Extracted from https://github.com/Altinn/altinn-studio/issues/6068. 
This issue should handle how we manage to solve this specific case. The input panel component should be used to present the information: #91 

**Case:** Some apps have a need to give the user the possibility to add information to a repeating group from another context. In this case inside a different repeating group. 

Example: User is presented with a repeating group where they are tasked with inputting credit cards. Later in the application they are presented with a dropdown list of all the credit cards they inputted earlier. The user now see that they forgot to include a card and would like to add the forgotten card in this context. When clicking the "legg til betalingskort" a empty credit card group is presented.

See more on figma: https://www.figma.com/file/wnBveAG2ikUspFsQwM3GNE/Altinn-Studio-Apps?node-id=15055%3A17514

## Alternative solutions
- Instead of filling out an element directly "inline" from a different context - would a button that takes you to the repeatin group be sufficient? Keep the `Legg til betalingskort` button, but that navigates you to the correct page? 
This would also solve the issue if the user see an error or just needs to edit one of the elements.

feature_sentence: As a user, I want validation: Present better error messages for required fields.
documentation_text: Source: https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/130 State: CLOSED Labels: kind/user-story, org/ssb Description: ## Description _As a user I want a clear description of the requirements that are needed to complete the form._ We need to explain in the text what field the error is about. Example: "You need to fill out your email address" instead of "This field is required". ## Design https://www.figma.com/file/Pvti3aRcOwH0k5Z7DrLznk/Arbeidsomr%C3%A5de%3A-Altinn-Studio-APPS?node-id=2545%3A50628 ## Possible solutions - Use a convention where texts with the same id as the corresponding data model element is used instead of the generic error texts. - Get the field-name from input label + generate requirements from json-schema? UPDATE: Displaying WHICH field should be completely doable, in that we can access information about the component and fetch the label text and add this in to the validation message. Displaying requirements for the field is not trivial to do consistently and well. Suggest that any such requirements that are important for the end user should be displayed elsewhere, f.ex. in a help text or description to the field and not in the error message. We also need to consider how we handle required field validation, as we have some custom behaviours that are not present for other kinds of validation (showing a banner with information about required fields, which turns red when there are missing required fields). Currently we loop through the available validation messages for the current view and pick up any that are for missing required fields. This might be difficult to do once we implement this issue, so we need to decide on how we structure information about missing required fields. Some options: - Continue as before, but make sure that the checks for if any required fields are missing in the view also handle more complex/detailed validation messages. - Add some property to the fields validations, like `missing`, to be sidelined with `errors` and `warnings` that we can use as a flag, instead of looping through validation errors. - Add a separate structure under `validations` in store to contain information about missing required fields for each view. Something similar to the `invalidData`-structure that we already have. ## Development tasks - [x] Consider possible solutions above. As a minimum we should tell the user which field is required. For example "Du må fylle ut fødselsnummer. ". But could we also include the requirements? For example: "Du må fylle ut fødselsnummer (11 siffer uten mellomrom)". - [ ] Decide how to structure info about missing required fields. - [ ] Implement solution - telling user which field is required in the error message by using field label text. ## Guidelines for app developers For custom validation messages, we should remind the app developer that they need to include keywords relating to the label in the validation message. "Dette feltet er påkrevd" Is not allowed. - [ ] Update [guidelines](https://docs.altinn.studio/app/design/guidelines/components/error-message/) for custom validation messages. ## Test ## Definition of done - [ ] Documentation (docs.altinn.studio) is updated (if relevant) - [ ] Technical documentation - [ ] User documentation - [ ] QA - [ ] Manual test is complete (if relevant) - [ ] Automated test is implemented (if relevant) - [ ] All tasks in this userstory are closed (i.e. remaining tasks are moved to other user stories or marked obsolete)

documentation_text: Source: https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/262 State: CLOSED Labels: area/process, status/ready-for-dev, Epic, kind/user-story, org/brg Description: ## Description After the backend now supports gateways frontend need to be updated to do the same ## Considerations - We need to update App API so that the app frontend knows that there are multiple flows out of the current task. Example. Go back to data from confirmation and confirm. Should also this API indicate if the user is authorized? - We need to design how the navigation buttons should be placed for returning to the previous task. - We need to design how the navigation buttons should be placed for forwarding - What if there are more than two flows out of a task. - Do we need a category of flows? - Think signing: Should it be a sign button on the back button, or should it maybe be a sign and deny sign? - What about authorization. Should buttons be disabled, or should we handle not authorized when clicking ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Frontend show button when a flow from the current task is present. This goes for both confirmation and feedback and possible data task. - [ ] An authorized user can press a button and instance state is then moved to the requested state - [ ] GUI for that given state is presented - [ ] Needed state change data updates are performed. (like unlocking data or deleting PDF) ## Specification tasks - [x] Altinn/app-frontend-react#271 - [ ] Altinn/app-frontend-react#97 - [x] Design GUI for the specific tasks. If needed. What if there are more than 2 options? - [x] Design GUI for what will happen when a user is not authorized to follow a specific flow. (Disabled button or warning when clicking) [Figma sketches](https://www.figma.com/file/wnBveAG2ikUspFsQwM3GNE/Altinn-Studio-Apps?node-id=15741%3A29639) - [x] Altinn/app-template-dotnet#129 - [ ] Development tasks are defined ## Design ### 1. If a user filled out a form, but **is not authorized** to confirm: **Preferred solution:** - The user can select from a list of authorized persons in the organization. The selected person(s) will recive a message in their innbox about a form ready to confirm. **Possible solution until notification is available:** - The user have to confirm that he understands that the data will **not** be sent, just saved for other in the organization with authorization to continue. - This will NOT be a good solution, since the user might not know who to contact in his organization to get this form signed/confirmed. To make this work, we have to show a static list of 1-3 autorized people in the organization. (When many authorized persons, could it pick someone who recently signed something else/was active?) ### 2. If a user filled out a form and **is authorized** to confirm: ### 3. If a user recive a form filled out by someone else, and has the permission to both **confirm** and **edit**: - A user with rights will see what the previous user filled out and be able to sign, change or send it back: ### 4. If a user receives a form filled out by someone else, and has the permission to **confirm** but not **edit**: **Preferred solution:** - The user will be able to send the form back to the person(s) who filled it out, and also add a comment on what is wrong/should be looked at again. **Possible solution until notification is available:** - When notification is not possible, the button "Send back" should not be visible. feature_sentence: As a user, I want design: Tables.
documentation_text: Source: https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/107 State: CLOSED Labels: ux, org/krt, kind/user-story, org/skd, org/ssb, org/pat, area/table, feature-complete Description: # Design: Tables To cover the service owner needs from [7273](https://github.com/Altinn/altinn-studio/issues/7273) we will create a new table component with the possibility of adding both static and editable cells. The tables should be used only when the information requires it: - When you have a large amount of data that requires to be arranged logically in rows and columns. - When you need to organize data that is too detailed or complicated to be described adequately in the text. - When the user needs to compare information between rows or columns, and quickly see the results. ## Design sprint tasks **Tasks that need to be done beforehand** - [x] Define scope of designsprint - [x] Structure the service owner needs from Altinn/altinn-studio#7273 They need to be handled in this sprint - [x] Create agenda for the designsprint - [x] Find similar solutions and inspiration - [x] Look into if we can get users for quick usertests ## Remaning tasks - [x] Finish up the design of the first version of tables - [ ] Land the scope of the first version of the table - [ ] Detailed specification - ready for development - [ ] Make design guidelines for the app developers on how to use the table correctly # Suggested scope There is no way that this component wont be a huge undertaking for the developers, but to minimize it a little we want to scope it down. So for the first version of the table we will not focus on the repeating aspect of table. (Letting the user add and remove rows themself.) ## Features we want to support in first version: **New** : Support static fields in table: Described in [#8491](https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/298) - **WCAG Requirements** - The component must meet all relevant requirements from WCAG. - **Validation** - If there are any validation rules, we need to follow the WCAG guidelines on how to help the user correct the fields that are failing. - **Responsiveness** - The table should work on all screen sizes with horizontal scroll in first version. - **Read-only table** - Present tabular data in a table that is not editable. - **Editable table** - The users should be able to edit the cells in the table. The cells should support inputfields, right-aligned inputfields (for numbers), dropdown (select) and checkboxes. - **Combination of read-only and editable cells**- Some cells will be pre-filled with data that the user cant edit. There needs to be a good visual indication on what cells the user can edit, and the cells that are read-only. - **Summation row** - One or more rows that show the calculation based on other values in the table. Should be presented as read-only fields and can be a row or a column. _Do they need to be read-only fields? Take another look at this!_ - **Header cells** - Up to two tier headers. The first [table example here](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/tables/irregular/) is a good example of what we need to support - **Dynamics** - Use dynamics to hide rows or columns that are are not important to the user. clarification: Should also be able to handle single rows. - **Prefilled rows** - Use a datasource to create the number of rows needed. You should also be able to set a value as the row header. (The column to the left) ## Features we are not supporting in this version - **Repeating tables** - The user can build the table. Adding and removing rows. - **Mobile version** - There should be made an optimized version for the smallest screens, where cells are stacked below each other. - **Zebra stripes** - For tables with a lot of data elements this will enhance the readablity of the table. - **Freezed columns** - For large data sets it could be helpfull to freeze a column to keep it visible as a user scroll horizontally. This will make it easier to know what the data belongs to and compare it. - **Pagination** - For larger tables this will be a must. A way to set a max visible rows and navigation for the user to go trough all the tables. - **Header sorting** - For larger tables. - **Filtering and search for end users** - The table will be static, we will not support searching or filtering in this version. - **Filtering for app owners** - Based on a user answer earlier in the process, some columns or cells should be possible to hide. - **On Paste** - Can we help the user to import information that is already in a table in another software, e.g. Excel. # Figma sketches https://www.figma.com/file/wnBveAG2ikUspFsQwM3GNE/Altinn-Studio-Apps?node-id=14756%3A10448 ## Design for first scope **Table example with:** - Inputfields, dropdown (select) and checkboxes - Right aligned text for numbers - Read-only cell - Summary row - Validation https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1464915/158565851-ceaaefed-ceab-4269-9a66-7e19e79a5f58.mov --- **Table example with:** - Scroll and expanded view https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1464915/156507329-ada6e5ee-1cae-45db-80ad-f04c7c33f9f5.mov --- **Table example with:** - Multiple header cells --- **Table example with:** - Dynamic cells https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1464915/156743172-a527c7f1-049e-4599-a4e0-fe2293775e2e.mov --- **Table example with:** - Mobile view https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1464915/156745035-e494f2ea-c83b-40e0-8a0e-0c4a882955c5.mov https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1464915/156747467-31a4f3a2-9cb1-494d-94ad-0958fa3f621c.mov --- ## Design for next scope **Table example with:** - Repeating tables https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1464915/156745656-21ef6fed-2d37-420c-b2bd-d3a67e0e8c03.mov If you want to encourage the user to make changes to the table, it should be set to edit mode by default. If the table has pre-filled data and the user is not to be prompted to edit, it can be set to view mode. The user will then have to press "Edit" to be able to make changes. --- **Table example with:** - Zebra stripes --- **Table example with:** - Pagination, search and sorting --- # Detailed specification ## Cell sizing The cells should as default have flexible witdh, and there should be a way to set a minimum width for each of the columns. ## Breakpoints ## Text adjustments ## Different start-modes for advanced table # Table Guidelines

Description:
## Description

For some application owners, it is better to show a designed view of the data and not pdf. See Altinn/apps-backlog#1 

## Screenshots
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13309071/140019711-8cbcd8b6-0f3d-49f9-a19f-43839322f124.png)

## Considerations

If we introduce a "confirmation view" design capability this might be used as input for a "receipt generated". This should be input to a more general "Do we need PDF" discussion. 

- Is there any need for components updates to be presented in this view?
- Can this be solved as a backend functionality? Generate HTML based on the layout and data and save it as data just like PDF?


## Analysis

Currently we support the following steps. Here data can be customized with formlayout as you wish, while the confirm step is static. 

```mermaid
stateDiagram
    direction LR
    [*] --> Data
    Data --> Confirm
    Confirm --> End
```

With the following process definition:

```xml
<bpmn2:process id="Altinn_Data_Confirmation_Process" isExecutable="false">
    <bpmn2:startEvent id="StartEvent_1">
      <bpmn2:outgoing>SequenceFlow_1</bpmn2:outgoing>
    </bpmn2:startEvent>
    <bpmn2:task id="Task_1" name="Fyll ut skjema" altinn:tasktype="data">
      <bpmn2:incoming>SequenceFlow_1</bpmn2:incoming>
      <bpmn2:outgoing>SequenceFlow_2</bpmn2:outgoing>
    </bpmn2:task>
    <bpmn2:task id="Task_2" name="Bekreft skjemadata" altinn:tasktype="confirmation">
      <bpmn2:incoming>SequenceFlow_2</bpmn2:incoming>
      <bpmn2:outgoing>SequenceFlow_3</bpmn2:outgoing>
    </bpmn2:task>
    <bpmn2:endEvent id="EndEvent_1">
      <bpmn2:incoming>SequenceFlow_3</bpmn2:incoming>
    </bpmn2:endEvent>
    <bpmn2:sequenceFlow id="SequenceFlow_1" sourceRef="StartEvent_1" targetRef="Task_1" />
    <bpmn2:sequenceFlow id="SequenceFlow_2" sourceRef="Task_1" targetRef="Task_2" />
    <bpmn2:sequenceFlow id="SequenceFlow_3" sourceRef="Task_2" targetRef="EndEvent_1" />
  </bpmn2:process>
```

The confirm step looks like this in the applicaiton:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10416981/188440537-b391f6b4-0ad5-4052-997e-9ccf912c1057.png)

BRG has a need to customize this view. How can we support this?

### Alt 1.

Keep the process as is: 

```mermaid
stateDiagram
    direction LR
    [*] --> Data
    Data --> Confirm
    Confirm --> End
```

But extend the `layout-sets.json` (see [docs](https://docs.altinn.studio/app/development/ux/pages/layout-sets/)) and make it possible to setup a layout set for the confirm step, where we would reference the datamodel in the previous step. Example configuration:

```json
{
    "sets": [
      {
        "id": "data-step",
        "dataType": "someDataModel",
        "tasks": [
          "Task_1"
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "custom-receipt",
        "dataType": "someDataModel",
        "tasks": [
          "Task_2"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
```

With the following app structure:

```
App:
| ....
├───ui
│   ├───custom-receipt
│   │   └───layouts
│   └───data-step
│       └───layouts
````

Changes needed:
- Frontend
  - If confirm step has setup a connected layout set => render.
  
### Alt 2.

As discussed in slack, another alternative would be to define a seperate data step that acts as a "Confirm" step.

```mermaid
stateDiagram
    direction LR
    [*] --> Data
    Data --> Data_2
    Data_2--> End
```

- What configuration would we need?
- What must be implemented to support re-using the same data model?
- How do we stay backward compat with existing applications using confirm (are there any?)

### Conclusion

After deliberation with the team + lead architect and our product owner we have landed on going forward with **Alt 1.**

### Altinn Studio

How can we add designer capabilities for different tasks? 

How can we map design to a given data model?  Do we need to? Can we make the assumption that it is a data model for the previous data task? 

What if the previous task had several data elements?

> Are there any requirements for monitoring? What is being built and what could go wrong? 
> Are there any requirements related to backup?

- Still possible to save something that can be used as proof?

feature_sentence: As a user, I want should checkboxes support true/false?.
documentation_text:
Source: https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/114

State: OPEN

Labels: ux, kind/user-story

Description:
## Description
We had an incident with an app with several checkbox-components, each with only 1 option to check. The data model fields were all booleans, so that checking the checkbox set the value to true. App: `digdir/godkjenn-bruksvilkaar`. 

However, after this change (from january 2021) https://github.com/Altinn/altinn-studio/commit/0bd246a09b82ea10c276567d43ec0970ae8e21ff#diff-df4b204405101ca09583792727c63870fcf2a486381a2575ca8eb334a33f2660, checkbox components no longer support toggling true/false. They only support toggling either options-value, or no value. 

In the specific incident mentioned above, this caused problems because the underlying data model fields were not nullable booleans, and when the data model was initialized, they were automatically set to `false`. Checking the checkbox then resulted in a value `false,true`, since toggling between true/false is not supported. This results in a validation error, since `false,true` is not a boolean value.

We need to decide if toggling true/false is behaviour we would expect from a checkbox, and if so, implement support for it.

## Screenshots
![InkedFeil i bruksvilkår_app (002)_LI](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1636323/123430551-9bdc1780-d5c8-11eb-9f68-62a21dd2dcfe.jpg)

## Considerations
Is togglig between true/false behaviour we expect from a checkbox? Or is this better covered by f.ex. a radiobutton (Yes/No), where the user actively has to choose? Is togglig between value/no value as we do now sufficient for a checkbox?

Description:
## Description
The application frontend will need to be able to parse and render the new text format consisting of pure key-value pairs.
The changing format is discussed in #378 

## Considerations
The new format has some substitution keys/values that might not be necessary to keep in memory/CDN once the application is published.
We have the Datamodel Variables (`dmv`) and the markdown-file references (`md`):
The `dmv` prefix can be converted to a `dm` prefixed datamodel-reference when deploying from studio.
- This will reduce the complexity of the frontend needing to know what is defined inside the `variables` files inside the app. 
- There will be no need to keep a copy of, (and maintain,) the `<datamodel>.varibales.json` files on CDN as they are only relevant for the App-developer.

## Not in scope
Markdown files can also be typed directly into the substitution variables when the application is deployed. This will also reduce the amount of complexity for the frontend.

## Disclaimer:
Below is the issue as defined September 15th 2020. Some of the instructions are therefore outdated. Consider #378 for an updated take on the format we will be using.

Ref. analysis from Altinn/altinn-studio#4450.
Standard texts should no longer be placed in app frontend, but should be fetched via API in the app, together with app texts.

## Screenshots
> Screenshots or links to Figma (make sure your sketch is public)

## Considerations
App already has API for fetching app texts. This already calls the storage API for fetching texts from storage It also caches the result, so that unnecessary calls to storage are not made, so we don't need to make changes to the API.

This could be a breaking change for app frontend, we will need to go to a new major version. This will allow apps using the current major version to continue to function, while apps using the new major version will need to update their text resources in order to work. Could we make a tool for this? Alternative is to add extra code to f.ex. convert old format to new during loading (or in storage?) for backwards compatibility. 

## Acceptance criteria
- Texts (both app texts and standard texts) are shown in app as expected.
- When an app is deployed, texts are updated

### Step 2
- We look into how we can make the messagebox receipt richer:
  - can we show the receipt view directly in the message box view instead of linking to it?
  - Could we leverage the existing correspondence functionality?
    - f.ex. provide the A3 inbox data on correnspondence format, so that we have the details directly available in the inbox item?
    - automatically create a corresponcence for the user with the receipt, and not show the instance itself? This would mean that the user cannot f.ex. create a copy of an archived instance.

Description:
## Description
We need to make sure that we support creating apps that will not have any App-Frontend as part of the app.  This is relevant when an app is ment to only be used from external API clients.  

For Sirus this is relevant since all interaction is done through APIs.

## PO Statement
This EPIC is related to Sirius who will create an app which shall only be available for end user systems through APIs. As this is the first app that will only be available to submit through API we need to have a look at how the user experience will be for creating apps without API. It is unknown how many apps that will be created without front end at this point, but it is expected that more apps will have this feature going forward.

## Tech statement
The app-architecture we have now is very limited, and it is limited because we've optimized the app code structure for "Studio UI first". This needs to be changed to an approach where Controllers, startup, etc. are part of the apps, so that APIs, CORS, auth, etc. can be added and tested/debugged directly by app developers.

## Considerations
- Should a developer choose actively when creating a new app what kind of template he want to create? Answer: Yes, in time, but not in Studio UI for MVP since api apps will be created by programmers in the short term.
- How are app logic accessed when not having App-Frontend? Answer: Through API.
- How can App-Frontend be added at a later stage. Answer: Add the missing files.
- Does it matter for App-Backend? Answer: Yes, app-backend needs drastic changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- Flow for creating a API-app is defined (api with only backend)
- Defined what kind of files that can be edited and are available. (no point enabling dynamics)
